description: §61.7 — paths at the edge of the grammar compile clean: a trailing `/` (an empty LAST segment), a segment that begins with `.` but is not `.` / `..`, every unreserved punctuation character, and `/_scrml_localx` (which only looks like the reserved `/_scrml_local/` prefix).
provenance: ruling:user-voice-scrml.md "⭐ RULED — S478 hand-off §3.A and §3.B, PA recs adopted (S479, 2026-11-18)" item 5 (`E-ENDPOINT-PATH-INVALID`; reserve `/_scrml_local/`)
rationale: §61.7: "A `path=` SHALL be an absolute path: it begins with `/`, and every other character is an RFC 3986 unreserved character (`A`–`Z`, `a`–`z`, `0`–`9`, `-`, `.`, `_`, `~`) or `/`. No segment is empty (`//`), `.` or `..` … A `path=` outside this grammar is `E-ENDPOINT-PATH-INVALID` (§61.9), reported at the `<endpoint>` opener." "a trailing `/` (an empty LAST segment) is allowed"; the reserved prefixes are `/_scrml_local` and paths beginning with `/_scrml_local/` only.
